editorial:
Imagine being such a pushy stage mom that you try to hire a hitman just because your daughter didn't make the cheerleading squad. That is exactly where you start with this wild ride. You get to see a Texas housewife who takes 'supportive parent' to a scary and hilarious extreme. The vibe is a mix of a dark comedy and a true crime story, making you laugh at how ridiculous the situation is while wondering how someone could actually think this was a good plan. It captures that sunny, superficial Texas lifestyle perfectly while showing the crazy secrets hiding behind the white picket fences.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the lead delivers a performance that is both terrifying and funny. The pacing stays quick, so you never feel bored as the plot twists and the police start closing in. While it is an older TV movie, the story holds up great. It is perfect for anyone who loves stories about suburban chaos and people who simply cannot handle losing. You will love how the tension builds up to the big crash.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the police finally catch up with the mom. After her crazy plan to kill the rival cheerleader fails, she is arrested and put on trial. The movie ends by showing how her obsession with her daughter's success ruined her life. You see her face the consequences of her crimes in court, proving that her desperate need for status was totally insane and not worth the prison time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crazy true stories and dark humor.
